rounds.response:
1) Pre‑deploy baselines to record (capture both "last 30m" and "7‑day median"): p95 latency (PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="payments-api",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le) )), total error rate % (PromQL: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="payments-api",env="prod",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="payments-api",env="prod"}[5m])) * 100), payment success rate (payments_success_count / payments_attempt_count over 30m), RPS and peak RPS, current replicas/pod status (kubectl get deploy/payments-api -n prod; kubectl get pods -l app=payments-api -n prod).  
2) Pass/hold/rollback thresholds: GREEN = within ±5% of 7‑day baseline and within hard SLOs (p95 ≤250ms, error <0.1%, payment success ≥99.9%); YELLOW (borderline) = p95 >+5% but ≤+25% vs baseline OR error rises above baseline but remains <0.1% OR payment success 99.7–99.9% → PAUSE for 15 minutes, run extended synthetics (see #4), notify SRE Lead + Release Manager, do not advance until metrics return to GREEN; RED (hard fail) = p95 >250ms OR error ≥0.1% OR payment success <99.7% OR any Sev‑1 → IMMEDIATE ROLLBACK.  
3) Gate checklist and signoffs (execute at each canary stage 1%→5%→25%→50%→100%): a) record baseline metrics (queries above) for last 30m and 7d median; b) run health checks: kubectl get pods -n prod && kubectl describe pod <any-crashing-pod> if needed; c) run Prometheus queries for p95, error%, payment success and confirm GREEN; d) scan recent logs: kubectl logs -l app=payments-api -n prod --tail=200 | grep -E "ERROR|WARN" and review; e) require explicit sign‑off in the ticket from SRE Lead + Release Manager to advance from each stage; Product Owner must approve before 100% cutover.  
4) Synthetic and security checks (extra for busy window 18:00–22:00 and at mid/post rollout): run ./scripts/synthetic_payment_test.sh --env=prod --partner=new --count=20 and confirm ≥99.9% success and p95 ≤250ms; Security Officer runs ./scripts/verify-logging-and-acls.sh --env=prod (or cloud logging query equivalent) at mid‑rollout and post‑rollout and capture audit log entries for the deploy window plus any IAM/role changes (example cloud queries: gcloud logging read or aws cloudtrail lookup-events templates in ticket); Security must sign off at mid‑rollout and before 100%.  
5) Rollback & escalation commands: on RED or any Sev‑1 run rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/payments-api -n prod (or ./ci/deploy.sh --rollback --service=payments-api), confirm pods return to Ready within the 2‑minute downtime tolerance, verify metrics return to baseline, and page SRE Lead + Release Manager + Incident Manager; do not resume ramp without their explicit approval and document all timeline/metric snapshots in the change ticket.
